title: Finite-dimensional normed spaces over locally compact normed fields are proper
statement: Let $K$ be a field [def-weil-field] with a multiplicative absolute value $|\cdot|:K\to\mathbf R_{\geq0}$, satisfying $|a|=0\iff a=0$, $|1|=1$, and $|a+b|\leq |a|+|b|$. Assume the absolute value is nontrivial (some nonzero $a$ has $|a|\ne1$) and $K$ is locally compact for $d(a,b)=|a-b|$. Let $Y$ be a $K$-vector space with a definite norm satisfying $\|ay\|=|a|\|y\|$ and $\|y+z\|\leq\|y\|+\|z\|$. If $Y$ is finite-dimensional [def-weil-finite-dimensional-subspace], then $Y$ is a proper metric space: every closed ball $\{y\in Y:\|y-c\|\leq r\}$, for $c\in Y$ and $r\in\mathbf R$, is compact in the norm topology. No completeness of $Y$ is assumed.
